description: CS Students previously experienced in using weather and vegetation data to build solutions for small-time farmers. Looking for enthusiasts in AI/AgriTech/ML and even Front-end Dev, the main goal is to learn and develop a real solution to a real problem
summary:
RoTerra is an explainable, farmer-centred decision-support tool for the NASA Space Apps "Field Shift" challenge. It helps farmers compare crop-rotation strategies that improve soil health and resilience to changing rainfall, heat, and water shortages. Many tools turn satellite data into black-box scores. RoTerra makes every recommendation traceable to its evidence.

The demo site is rice farming in the Colusa Basin of California's Sacramento Valley. The app has four modules. Users can understand local climate risk through trends, compare at least four rotation strategies, reveal the tradeoffs behind each score, and see the uncertainty in every indicator. Farmers set their own priorities, such as water, income, and soil, with sliders. A rule-based weighted scoring engine then ranks the options. It is deliberately not machine learning, and 35 tests pass.

The app uses NASA POWER and Landsat data, plus OpenET, USDA CDL crop history and SSURGO soil data. It is built with React, Vite, Leaflet and Recharts, and runs from static JSON with no backend. It is open source and live at roterra. earth. Malaysian paddy is planned as the next adaptation.

RoTerra supports farmer judgment and does not replace it. Crop trait scores are illustrative and flagged as needing local review.
details:
Project Details: RoTerra

What it does and how it works

RoTerra is an explainable crop-rotation explorer. It helps farmers decide what to plant next as rainfall, heat, and water supply change. The demo plot is a rice field in the Colusa Basin of California's Sacramento Valley.

The app has four modules:

  • Understand Risk: shows observed climate and vegetation trends for the plot, with source and uncertainty labels.
  • Compare Rotations: scores at least four rotation strategies against the farmer's own priorities. These are water, income, soil health, pest pressure and equipment. The farmer sets the priorities with sliders.
  • Reveal Tradeoffs: lets users expand any score into a per-dimension breakdown and the data behind it.
  • Make Uncertainty Visible: an evidence drawer lists the source, resolution and confidence of each indicator.

A Python pipeline fetches the data and writes static JSON files, and the React app reads them. Scoring is a rule-based weighted matrix. Observed trends, such as a rainfall shift, adjust the weights. Satellite data therefore drives the ranking and doesn't just decorate it. Results fall into four bands: Strong fit, Promising, Needs review and Not advised now.

Benefits

  • Farmers can see why each option is suggested, not only which one ranks first.
  • It turns fragmented Earth-observation data into a clear next step.
  • It shows what is uncertain and doesn't hide it.
  • It is free, open source, and works without a backend or database.

Intended impact

RoTerra aims to support better soil health, water conservation and income resilience. It is a support tool only and never replaces farmer judgment or extension officers. The framework is built to adapt to other regions. Malaysian paddy (Sekinchan) is the planned first international adaptation, using sources that already cover Malaysia, such as NASA POWER.

Tools and technology

  • Frontend: React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, daisyUI, Leaflet (map), Recharts (charts) and a three.js globe.
  • Data pipeline: Python scripts that output static JSON.
  • NASA data: NASA POWER and Landsat, accessed through Microsoft Planetary Computer.
  • Other data: OpenET, USDA Cropland Data Layer (crop history) and USDA SSURGO (field-scale soil).
  • Testing and deployment: 35 passing scoring-engine tests, ESLint, and GitHub Actions deploying to GitHub Pages at roterra.earth.
  • AI assistance: used for code guidance and drafting text. It is disclosed in the repo, and all output was reviewed and edited by the team.

No special hardware was used.

Creativity

Most tools in this space are black-box or purely descriptive. RoTerra makes explainability the core of the design. The scoring is rule-based on purpose, every number links to evidence, and uncertainty is shown openly. The farmer's priorities shape the ranking, so the tool doesn't impose one "best" answer. The product design also keeps the same crop, rice, across sites. That gives it a direct route from the US demo to Malaysian paddy.

Factors considered

  • Scientific integrity: we removed fabricated forecast content and list only datasets that are actually integrated. Planned ones (IMERG, SMAP, ECOSTRESS, PRISM) are marked optional.
  • Resolution: each dataset's resolution is stated honestly. For example, SMAP is coarse at about 9 km.
  • Agronomic limits: crop trait scores are illustrative and flagged as needing local review.
  • Trust and use: the tool supports farmers and doesn't replace them. Simple controls keep it usable.
  • Openness: all sources are cited, the code is open source, and AI use is disclosed.
